positions.as_written: Use varus stress radiography where the grade decides the treatment.
Examine under anaesthetic, because lateral findings are subtler than medial ones.
Assess alignment, since varus loads the lateral structures in stance.
Treat lateral laxity as the finding that is harder to detect and more consequential than its medial counterpart, because the structures heal badly and the alignment usually works against them.
Measure alignment before planning a lateral reconstruction.
Use varus stress radiography rather than grading by hand where the treatment turns on it.
Expect the lateral structures to stretch rather than heal.
